text:
elaine: hey — running into a weird 401 when calling the Redwood API from our node service. header code is:
```
const auth = `Basic ${Buffer.from(`${process.env.API_KEY}:`).toString('base64')}`
fetch(url, { headers: { Authorization: auth } })
```
works when i curl locally with the same base64 string, but in prod on a Windows container it 401s. any ideas?

mark: ugh Windows env weirdness. first check: is there any trailing newline/CRLF or hidden char in the env var (clipboard copy from a manager can sneak one in). easiest: print hex of the raw bytes and compare. on linux/mac: `printf "%s" "$API_KEY" | xxd -p -c 256`

jp: on pwsh you can do a quick hex dump: `([System.Text.Encoding]::UTF8.GetBytes($env:API_KEY)) -join ' '` or `Write-Output $env:API_KEY | Format-Hex` — watch out for 0d (CR) at the end.

elaine: great call — when I hex-dumped i see `0d 0a` at the end. so CRLF was in the secret. odd though, GH Actions secret is set via UI (no CRLF). the dev container probably got it via a .env file created on Windows.

sarah: yep, .env files created with Notepad often get CRLF. two quick fixes: trim in code (`process.env.API_KEY?.replace(/\r|\n/g, '')`) or write secrets into files with LF only. also in GH Actions use `echo -n "${{ secrets.API_KEY }}" > file` to avoid newline.

mark: also watch for hidden zero bytes if someone pasted with weird clipboard — `tr -d '\0'` or `sed` can help. base64 length mismatch vs curl is a tell: `echo -n "$API_KEY" | wc -c` should match what you expect.

elaine: fixed by trimming `replace(/\r|\n/g, '')` before base64. thanks. i left a quick note in the repo README about generating secrets on Windows. :thumbsup:

devops-bot: Note: rotated API key for envs where CRLF secrets were detected. Follow-up: if you hatched a rollout, check pods for restarts.

jp: one more small thing — for Node http libs that auto-normalize headers, ensure `Authorization` isn't getting lowercased or duplicated. i usually log `req.getHeader('authorization')` in a debug route when investigating.

elaine: good tip, will add a debug route temporarily. thanks everyone!
